req.title: Posts include author username
req.statement: The system shall join post rows with users so index/detail responses include the author's username.

doc.reasoning: The requirement specifies that the system should include the author's username in the post responses. This involves ensuring that the database join operation between posts and users is correctly implemented and that the API response includes the expected data. The test suite will cover positive, negative, and boundary cases to ensure robustness against common mutations.

tests.name: test_posts_include_author_username_positive
preconditions: Database is initialized with a user and a post.
actions: Send a GET request to the '/' endpoint.
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
client = app.test_client()

with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db, get_db
    init_db()
    db = get_db()
    db.execute("INSERT INTO user (id, username, password) VALUES (1, 'testuser', 'testpass')")
    db.execute("INSERT INTO post (id, title, body, author_id) VALUES (1, 'Test Title', 'Test Body', 1)")
    db.commit()

r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200
assert b'testuser' in r.data

tests.name: test_posts_include_author_username_negative
preconditions: Database is initialized without any posts.
actions: Send a GET request to the '/' endpoint.
expected: Response does not include any posts
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
client = app.test_client()

with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db
    init_db()

r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200
assert b'No posts yet' in r.data or b'[]' in r.data

tests.name: test_posts_include_author_username_boundary
preconditions: Database is initialized with a user and a post with maximum allowed title length.
actions: Send a GET request to the '/' endpoint.
expected: Response includes the author's username and the post with maximum title length
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
client = app.test_client()

max_title_length = 255
long_title = 'T' * max_title_length

with app.app_context():
    from flaskr.db import init_db, get_db
    init_db()
    db = get_db()
    db.execute("INSERT INTO user (id, username, password) VALUES (1, 'testuser', 'testpass')")
    db.execute("INSERT INTO post (id, title, body, author_id) VALUES (1, ?, 'Test Body', 1)", (long_title,))
    db.commit()

r = client.get('/')
assert r.status_code == 200
assert b'testuser' in r.data
assert long_title.encode() in r.data
